To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conversion coefficients of some γ-transitions in 201Tl and 203Tl were determined by means of simultaneous measurement of γ-quanta and conversion electron spectra employing intensity calibrated semiconductor γ-detectors.
we have measured conversion coefficients for the 331 keV and 361 keV transitions in201Tl as well as for the 279 keV in203Tl.
we determined the penetration parameters of internal conversion and the mixing ratios of theM 1 transitions in the nuclei201Tl and 203Tl.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the penetration parameters of internal conversion for someM 1-γ-transitions in the isotopes201Tl and 203Tl.
the study of the internal conversion and the E2-beimischung for theM 12 transitions in 201Tl and 203Tl.
a precise determination of the penetration parameters of inner conversion and E2 admixtures in the case ofM 1 transitions in201Tl (331 keV) and203Tl (279 keV).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present results are in agreement with the theoretical predictions.

the experimental values of the conversion coefficients for the 361 keV and the 279 keV transitions in201Tland203Tl, respectively, agree with the theoretical values within the limits of experimental error.
the experimental data are in agreement with the theoretical calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental data are in good agreement with theoretical predictions and with the data of other authors.
the results for the ℓ forbidden transitions agree with the predictions of the theory.
we have determined the internal conversion parameters for the first time with sufficient precision to test the theory of internal conversion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conversion coefficients and conversion ratios are very sensitive to the mixing ratio δ2.

the penetration parameters λ of the ℓ-forbiddentransitions can be measured with a precision of about ± 1.0 and that this precision is sufficient for the calculation of the nuclear matrix elements for these transitions.
the penetration parameter λ is not very sensitive to the multipole mixing ratio.
